title: Are there people making games here that come from a art/animation background ?
author: cybercafe6
selftext:
People using ai to build games is awesome but I've noticed most of them are programmers or people who never did art in the first place and seek to automate most of the art generation so I was wondering if there are people in this sub who make assets on their own and come from a background of art and not programming.

 Personally since the art community is very touchy about this I had to keep all my game Dev with ai activities to myself to not tarnish my reputation, is anyone feeling the same?

I wish I could just fully be open about it without closing doors.

Thx!

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body:
I come from a music background and have been using ai to program and half making half generating arts. Just using ai to fill in the gaps I’m bad at but still trying to improve in those. Would like to see myself be doing all my own art at some point. 

Against popular belief, do do think generating art then editing is teaching me a great deal because at first I was only generating and the further I get into my project the more I’m doing myself.

Learning to code so far is what I have the least interest in but I’m still trying to pick up some stuff. I could be wrong but I don’t think coding is going to be what it used to be in 5/10 years. Especially for games. It just kind of feels like a waste of time to fully learn how to boomer code when I rather focus on art, music and game design.

replies.author: cybercafe6
replies.body:
yeah! actually fixing generations can really work especially if youve got enough of a coherent art style to work off of. i attempted to use the art i made as reference in new asset generations that i can use either as layout for trying this out or just patching up to be up to my standard. but thus far i really have to be about how i want it to be so it doesn't turn to slop. 

as a non coder, learning to program just gives you the opportunity to make a more stable architecture to support your work long term i feel. thus far it feels like my creativity comes up with ways i want to work and i have to understand fundemental concepts in programing and computing in order reliably architect, if i completely turn a blind eye it usually comes falling down quite quickly and feels super brittle.

but in the end if the code works, it works. and thats why i feel like most ai made games just lack that personal touch cause they lack some sort of art fundementals. I assume you make the music for your game yourself? thus far for music, i have heard ai generated music that i liked but it didnt feel as personal and unique as some of my favorite tracks.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body:
Yeah I have been making my own music and own sound fx actually. Because I already did that in the past so it’s what I know. I haven’t messed around with ai music and sound stuff.

Not saying I don’t wanna learn more about code. I try my best to understand what the ai is doing and when I can do something manually in godot’s editor I usually learn how to do it until I have it in memory. But now I even have ai do stuff I already know because it’s faster.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
there are some for sure. I remember commenting on a post where the dev is a graphics designer. he/she makes a game about dreams and I remember the UIs looking pretty good 

you can always spawn a different "persona" for your aigamedev. Just don't attach your name to your aigamedev stuff if you really want to be able to just drop it one day with no strings attached

I just kept the same [itch.io](http://itch.io) etc when I transition to aigamedev since my non-ai gamedev era wasn't all that impressive anyways

good luck

comments.author: Both_Alternative890
comments.body: To be honest, with AI a good consistent art is more problematic thing than code.

comments.author: erofamiliar
comments.body:
I don't know if I count because I've always been more of a hobbyist, but I'm more of a 3D modeler/animator than I am a programmer. I love fixing up models, but AI generated models, while useful for some things, aren't exactly what I want. Good for reference, though! And AI generated animation is fine, but I'd rather do most of the animation by hand myself so it looks consistent. When I do use AI for the art it's mostly to generate references or images to stencil on as textures, and since I target PSX-looking stuff, that works for me.

...And then after all of that, like 90% of what I have so far is [itch.io](http://itch.io) assets anyway, lol. And I'm so far off from anything I can actually release, I only just got the first enemy working. But with AI doing most of the heavy lifting with code it's coming together nicely! I can spend a single day making assets, and then only a single day wiring all of those assets up. With AI I got dismemberment working in only a couple of hours, and I'm using vertex shading for old-school PSX style blood stains in enemies and now I've got the blood stains transferring from the original character to the dismembered mesh, using GDExtension so it's much more performant than it would've been. Doing that all on my own would've taken weeks.

And it helps that like square yam says down below, I'm using a different persona for this stuff. I don't really hav a public image to tarnish. But when I do have a project I want to release, my plan is to be as open and transparent about the AI use as possible. I feel like people get FURIOUS when they think AI has been smuggled in, but it's hard to care about the 1000s of games openly using it.

replies.author: cybercafe6
replies.body: i see! i definitely get you about doing the anims yourself. for most people animation is a pain point but for me its a way to give it personality. i think transparency is important right now for release but in the long term it feels a bit weird to have to explicitely say since lots of games use it to varying degrees. to me its like admitting that i used a camera to make a film but i know lots of people would disagree. adding that extra disclosure is honest but i feel it can also hurt potential players cause they might think its less authentic (depends on the target audience). if your game is truly unique it feels like shooting yourself in the foot a bit but for the time being, its probably the move until its more customary. but id like to believe that even if theres a ai disclosure if the game looks bomb people would still try it.

replies.author: erofamiliar
replies.body:
I do think that if the game is sick, people will complain about the AI but they won't really *care*, like something like ARC Raiders got a ton of complaints but it still raked in money and has a huge supportive audience. They're replacing some of the voices with actors *now*, but this is happening after the game was already hugely successful.

But I also think hiding the use of AI hurts creators that use AI because it contributes to the survivorship bias thing. A great game that uses AI openly can help shift popular opinion, whereas if the only games that openly use AI are the ones people associate with AI slop, then that's the view that's gonna stick. If people hide AI use only for it to get discovered later, that further contributes to the idea that AI use is this shameful deceptive *thing* and that the only people who use it are grifters and thieves.

I'm also just big on pro-consumer stuff and when a ton of people care about the AI, it's better to let folks make an informed decision than smuggle it in.

replies.author: cybercafe6
replies.body: yeah i think youre right... hehe thanks for changing my mind.

comments.author: Fun_Worry_3079
comments.body: Not from an animation background but, before I became a game designer, I was a graphic designer (mostly for a hobby). I use PixelLab to create my assets, but I always make sure to perform pixel cleanup in Aesprite (now that I’m more proficient with the software).

comments.author: jackadgery85
comments.body:
I make ai art for fun.

For 20 years prior, I've made digital art for fun.

For 5 years prior, I've made small, simple games for fun. One of them has a mix of my art, my childhood friend's art, and minimal early ai art. 

For my whole remembered life, I've made art of various kinds. Ai art is only different in method. Same creative intent. Same conceptual style that I'm comfortable with exploring.
